problemStatement:
A steel-frame chair carries dead load from its own weight, live load from an ordinarily seated occupant, and accidental load when a person lands heavily on the seat. The accidental case is represented by a given 6.0 kN equivalent-static vertical design load; students do not derive it from impact kinematics.

The seat is idealized as transferring load equally to two equivalent transverse rails. One rail is modeled as a fixed-fixed beam with a centered point load and an instructor-assigned square hollow steel section. These details are teaching assumptions, not measurements or verified construction features of a photographed chair.
engineeringGoal: Use the specified 6.0 kN accidental vertical seat load to determine the bending stress in one idealized rail, calculate factor of safety, determine the maximum allowable total accidental load, and assess whether the rail meets the required strength criterion.
